_comment: CANONICAL cross-repo fixtures for terminology drift (§3.9).
Every note below is REAL, copied from NLM's live SPARQL endpoint on 2026-08-01,
because the format varies more than any spec suggests: two-digit years (84(77),
1975-93), 'for A use B' forms where B is the heading to search, multiple clauses
in one note, and notes whose leading year disagrees with dateIntroduced.
What is deliberately NOT parsed: the note's own leading year (it sometimes
contradicts dateIntroduced, and picking a winner would be inventing a fact) and
the 'for A' concept in a 'for A use B' clause. `hasUnparsedText` reports honestly
that something in the note went uninterpreted, and the raw note always travels

noteCases.name: prior heading with a full year range
two-digit end year expands to the 20th century
two-digit leading years are ignored, not misread as headings
noteCases.note: 84(77); for DNA POLYMERASE ALPHA use DNA POLYMERASE II 1982-97

noteCases.name: in 'for A use B', B is the heading to search
noteCases.note: 2023; for DATA SOURCES use INFORMATION STORAGE AND RETRIEVAL 1986-2022

noteCases.name: a single year means one year, not an open range
noteCases.note: 2023; use Health Disparity, Minority and Vulnerable Populations 2022

priorHeadings.heading: Health Disparity, Minority and Vulnerable Populations

noteCases.name: two clauses in one note both parse
a bare year note names no prior heading
a parenthesised year note names no prior heading
an empty note parses to nothing

driftCases.name: a 2014 heading cannot reach a search that starts in 1990
driftCases.messageMatches: Records from 1990–2013 were never indexed with it

driftCases.name: with no date limit the gap is everything before the heading existed
a heading with no replacement says free text is the only route
a heading with a replacement names it and its years
a search starting at the introduction year loses nothing
driftCases.messageMatches: nothing is lost to terminology here

driftCases.name: a 1966 heading is baseline, never a gap
no introduction date is unknown, not assumed safe
driftCases.messageMatches: Look it up in the MeSH Browser

queryCases.name: the history query asks for exactly the two predicates that exist
